name: Engineering Career

claims.claim_text: A consulting practice can start as moonlighting alongside employment: two years of part-time work for a single client, carried out with the employer's knowledge, preceded the move to full time, and the work was priced well below its market rate throughout that period.
claims.quote_verbatim: I had the same client for the two years I was moonlighting
claims.speaker: Scott Williams
claims.episode_title: Design & Manufacturing Consulting with Scott Williams from Xentronics

claims.claim_text: Access to the IEEE paper archive is normally bought by an institution; an engineer without an academic or employer subscription faces a five-figure annual cost, so leaving that affiliation cuts off the literature.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to pay like 30 grand to access all that
claims.episode_title: Cultural Differences

claims.claim_text: Sales roles are paid a commission on each unit sold while the engineer who designed the product has no equivalent share of its revenue; earning materially more than a salary from engineering work therefore requires owning and selling the product rather than being paid to design it.
claims.quote_verbatim: How do you pay a commission back to someone who designed it?
claims.episode_title: Girl Power

claims.claim_text: Engineers wanting to move into a different area of electronics commonly ask whether further study will open the path; the answer given from years of fielding the question is that changing employer accomplishes the move and additional coursework generally does not.
claims.quote_verbatim: Just get out and go and get another job
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: China, Entrepreneurs and Blue Collar Reality

claims.claim_text: Analog and integrated-circuit designers are both scarce and comparatively well paid, and a completed silicon design presented at interview is decisive portfolio evidence in that specialism.
claims.quote_verbatim: Go and make a chip and then take it to the interview
claims.episode_title: Analog Components, First Person Flying and Idea Ownership

claims.claim_text: Mathematics taught as central to an engineering degree may go unused in practice: more than twenty years in industry passed without a single occasion to use an integral, the applicability depending heavily on the area worked in.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've been in the industry for more than 20 years. I, you know, I'm yet to use an integral
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Bob Widlar, Electronic Design, FIRST Robotics - Monday, Meta Monday

claims.claim_text: An unfinished degree - four years of electrical engineering stopped three courses short of completion - steered a career away from salaried employment and toward independent work, on the assumption that employers would screen the missing credential out.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've stayed away from having real jobs because I figured no one would hire me
claims.speaker: Jack Ganssle
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jack Ganssle - Embedded Elchee Epexegesis

claims.claim_text: United States compensation as stated around 2011: a senior engineer earned a six-figure salary against a median family income of $51,000 for an entire household. In Australia six figures was attainable but marked out an engineer as doing well rather than typical.
claims.quote_verbatim: once you become a senior engineer, you're making a six-figure salary
claims.speaker: Jack Ganssle
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jack Ganssle - Embedded Elchee Epexegesis

claims.claim_text: Falling entry into engineering compounds as the existing workforce ages, producing a persistent shortage that favours practising engineers and leaves employers competing for them.
claims.quote_verbatim: there will be an ever-increasing shortage
claims.speaker: Jack Ganssle
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jack Ganssle - Embedded Elchee Epexegesis

claims.claim_text: An Australian engineering pay slip from about twenty years before 2011 recorded an hourly rate of $11.6396.
claims.quote_verbatim: I used to earn $11.6396 per hour
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Open Orbific Oratiuncle

claims.claim_text: Engineering students build their picture of industry from fellow students and academic staff alone, and academic staff are unrepresentative of working engineers, so the picture is distorted until direct contact with practising engineers corrects it.
claims.quote_verbatim: professors are so far from your working engineer that your view of the world is so distorted
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Jersey Jeff Jactitation

claims.claim_text: Work prepared before it is formally requested lets an engineer deliver immediately when the request arrives; internal standing at an employer is set by a small number of such visible events and persists for the remainder of the engineer's time at that company.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get that rep for the rest of your career at that company
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Distribution, Wozniak & Robots - Early Eight-bit Endgame

claims.claim_text: Engineers move into management to gain control over decisions they watch being made badly, and the move trades away the hands-on technical work that motivated it.
claims.quote_verbatim: But you have to give up stuff in order to do so
claims.episode_title: Project Management, Lasers & Robots - Staunch Specialty Sanctanimity

claims.claim_text: In-house product development frequently ends in cancellation, so an employed engineer may spend six months or more on work that never reaches a market; the stated reason for leaving employment was that independent work produces output that actually ships.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'd be working on something for six months and then it'd just get shit canned
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Project Management, Lasers & Robots - Staunch Specialty Sanctanimity

claims.claim_text: Hand-packing and shipping kits maximises profit per unit but converts the business into a twelve-hour-a-day job with substantial revenue and little margin, so labour-intensive self-employment is not an escape from salaried hours.
claims.quote_verbatim: You've just scored yourself a 12 hour a day job for the rest of your life
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, IndieGoGo & Ignite - Jasperated Jimswinger Jobbery

claims.claim_text: Technical support was a common entry route into engineering roles at SparkFun because support work demands deep product knowledge; the consequence for the employer is that the support team continually loses its best staff to engineering.
claims.quote_verbatim: he keeps hiring good people, and then they leave for an engineering
claims.episode_title: An Interview with the SparkFun Team - Efficacious Engineering Ensemble

claims.claim_text: Demand for one engineer's work changed when microcontroller programming was added to circuit building: discrete-logic and analog projects drew no paid requests, while the ability to program in assembly produced paid odd jobs and eventually an offer of employment.
claims.quote_verbatim: people did care all of a sudden once I could program an assembly
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Todd Bailey - Embedded Embrasure Engineering

claims.claim_text: Toy design at one employer ran at roughly eighty-hour weeks sustained over several years.
claims.quote_verbatim: thus began a bunch of 80-hour work weeks for many years of my life designing toys
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Todd Bailey - Embedded Embrasure Engineering

claims.claim_text: A reported 40 percent of women holding engineering degrees either leave the profession or never enter it; no comparable figure for men was available, and the discussion noted that a control group is needed before the number can be interpreted.
claims.quote_verbatim: 40% of women with engineering degrees either leave the profession or never enter the field
claims.episode_title: Travel Recaps and Altium Announcements - Artisinal Aussie Assemblage

claims.claim_text: Workload expectations differ sharply between engineering employers and circulate by reputation within a local industry; the difference appears in hours worked rather than in output delivered.
claims.quote_verbatim: they just grind their people down
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Wrong Hardware, Wrong Software - Fugacious Fan Funding

claims.claim_text: Short tenures count against a candidate when a resume is read, so engineers commonly stay in a poorly fitting job for at least nine months to a year before moving.
claims.quote_verbatim: you want to stay at least that long in a job so it looks decent on your resume
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Wrong Hardware, Wrong Software - Fugacious Fan Funding

claims.claim_text: Large companies hire new graduates readily and grow more reluctant as a candidate's experience accumulates, because the experienced applicant is more expensive and less easily directed; the route proposed is to take the large-company job first for the training it provides and go independent later.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's probably easier as a young person to get hired into a big company right now
claims.speaker: Bob Davidson
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: In an interview the question asking a candidate to describe their ideal job is scored against the role on offer rather than treated as an open question.
claims.quote_verbatim: The answer is always this exact job you just described to me
claims.speaker: Elecia White
claims.episode_title: Is This A Show?

claims.claim_text: Running a funded company means taking on the work of raising money, which cannot be combined with continuing to practise engineering.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you want to keep being an engineer, you don't get to go hunting for money
claims.episode_title: Standing With Ahmed

claims.claim_text: Completing a combined university and company training programme does not guarantee technical work at the end of it: the positions offered were office roles whose day-to-day content had little to do with electrical engineering.
claims.quote_verbatim: The jobs which were offered were just office jobs where you do things that most of the time don't have much to do with electrical engineering
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Great Scott

claims.claim_text: Roughly five years spent in a university post or other work isolated from industrial practice is reported to make a candidate unattractive to industry employers, and a full-time content-creation record carries the same uncertainty when presented to a company.
claims.quote_verbatim: after five years, you're pretty much become unattractive for the industry
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Great Scott

claims.claim_text: An engineer returning to a university department after years in industry found the curriculum unchanged from his own student years: the same topics, the same designs and the same textbooks.
claims.quote_verbatim: things really hadn't changed since I was a student
claims.speaker: Clint Cole
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: The United States responds to its engineering shortfall by importing engineers and exporting jobs, but the same shortage is reported in Australia and Western Europe, so the labour is not simply relocating between regions.
claims.quote_verbatim: We're importing engineers and exporting jobs
claims.speaker: Clint Cole
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: Free or cheap design tools and low-cost prototyping have raised the output of a single engineer to what was previously ten people's work over the same period, which masks a workforce shortfall rather than removing it.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can do a job today that would have taken 10 people 10 years ago
claims.speaker: Clint Cole
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: Degreed engineers with around three years of experience expect between $90,000 and $200,000 a year, which places board-level consumer repair below the wage they will accept and leaves that work to trained non-engineers earning $40,000 to $50,000.
claims.quote_verbatim: they want to make $90,000 to $200,000 a year to be an engineer
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: Entry into Silicon Valley engineering without any college degree was achieved through demonstrated delivery, building a reputation as the person to approach to get a design finished.
claims.quote_verbatim: started doing engineering without any college degree
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: Jeri Ellsworth and the demise of CastAR

claims.claim_text: A company that completed a commercial product still failed to sell it because none of the people running it could sell; the missing commercial function, rather than the technology, ended the business.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm not a very good salesperson. I'm more of a developer
claims.speaker: Julia Truchsess
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Julia Truchsess

claims.claim_text: Taking electronics as both hobby and occupation removed the hobby, because the working day consisted of the same activity that had been the recreation.
claims.quote_verbatim: somehow I lost my hobby because I did the same thing more or less the whole day
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Andreas Spiess

claims.claim_text: Electrical and firmware engineering forms a small community within any one region, and the same people recur across a career, which is the mechanism behind referral-driven hiring and the reason a badly ended relationship follows an engineer.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't want to burn any bridges in this area because you're going to run across the same people that you met earlier on in life
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: Defence work carries documentation and procurement overhead that consumes the engineer's time in place of design: two weeks spent specifying a single screw is given as representative of the work.
claims.quote_verbatim: you spend two weeks specifying a screw
claims.episode_title: The Almighty Dollarydoo

claims.claim_text: Graduates of the most prestigious engineering schools are largely absent from ordinary industry hiring pools - across an entire career of interviewing in Sydney none from the city's flagship university appeared - because those graduates are recruited separately through campus job fairs by employers competing for them.
claims.quote_verbatim: Have I ever met or interviewed or seen a resume of an engineer from the university of Sydney
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Drab Olive

claims.claim_text: The test proposed for going independent early in a career, around the five-year mark, is whether mentors and people to learn from remain reachable outside an employer, since access to them is the main thing employment otherwise supplies.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you think you can go out on your own and still find mentors and find people to interact with and learn from, then that's fine
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Chip Shortage Denier

claims.claim_text: Where a degree course is taught theoretically and leaves hands-on electronics outside the coursework, practical experience has to be obtained separately; in one case it came from working at Intel, Fujitsu and several startups concurrently with study.
claims.quote_verbatim: I worked at Intel. I worked for some startups and I worked at Fujitsu all while studying
claims.speaker: Shrouk El Attar
claims.episode_title: Creative Engineering with Shrouk El-Attar

claims.claim_text: A consulting side business goes dormant when its principal holds a full-time job and is also studying; the practice does not sustain itself without time allocated to it.
claims.quote_verbatim: my consulting stuff is not so much these days
claims.speaker: Paul Zawada
claims.episode_title: The Smart Grid with Paul Zawada

claims.claim_text: Clients hire consultants on the strength of accumulated employed experience, so consulting is not an entry-level path; experience of both large and small organisations broadens what the consultant can offer.
claims.quote_verbatim: they didn't do that out of college. They've gone and earned their stripes somewhere
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Siloed Engineering with Leigh Brady

claims.claim_text: A graduate degree can act as an admission filter to the applicant pool rather than as a requirement for the work itself; in engineering a bachelor's degree is sufficient for most roles, whereas neighbouring sciences require a doctorate to be considered at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think I could do the work without the degree completely
claims.speaker: Joshua Vasquez
claims.episode_title: Grad School Time Capsule with Joshua and Zach

claims.claim_text: PCB layout capability is becoming widely available, which improves access but weakens it as a differentiator when selling engineering services; firmware is judged to hold the harder remaining problems, and is therefore the safer skill to deepen.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm not sure it's as hireable
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: A Noisy Rude Bus

claims.claim_text: Career planning changes shape with experience: a year or two out of school the plan is a specific job title to hold within five years, and after roughly ten years and several job changes that target is replaced by broader criteria such as being a capable and trusted resource.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was probably after about 10 years that I stopped having that as my, my, my end point or my plan
claims.episode_title: Engineering Careers with Circuit Break & James Lewis

claims.claim_text: Choosing career moves primarily by the people available to learn from is offered as the most reliable single criterion, explicitly qualified as advice from someone late in career with choices available; a person starting out who needs the income should take the income first.
claims.quote_verbatim: just following talent of people to learn from
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Electric Propulsion with Todd Bailey
